ambiguities: The standard finite-function norm selected by Pi.normedRing is the supremum norm, hence the maximum absolute coordinate for these nonempty finite index sets. Its underlying seminorm construction is referenced but not expanded at the supplied frontier.
Fin.foldl is the standard increasing-index left fold. Its body delegates to an unexpanded private loop; the sequential recurrence below uses that standard meaning.

The error variables specify an abstract multiplicative real-arithmetic model. The proposition does not specify a floating-point format, rounding rule, representability condition, overflow behavior, or underflow behavior.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the computed vector whose componentwise relative errors and relative supremum-norm error are bounded.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every natural n, real vectors x and δexp indexed by 0,…,n, an addition-error vector δadd indexed by 0,…,n−1, a division-error vector δdiv indexed by 0,…,n, and j in 0,…,n, define ŷ_j = (w_j/S)(1+δdiv_j), where w is D004 and S is D003. This definition itself imposes no error bounds or nonzero-denominator hypothesis.
dependency_coverage.name: Computed normalized exponential vector

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines the exact comparison vector y and the denominator of the relative norm error.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every natural n, x:{0,…,n}→ℝ and j in that index set, define y_j = exp(x_j)/(Σ_{i=0}^n exp(x_i)).
dependency_coverage.name: Exact normalized exponential vector

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Fixes the summation algorithm and where each addition error acts in the computed denominator.
dependency_coverage.meaning: For every natural n, x,δexp:{0,…,n}→ℝ and δadd:{0,…,n−1}→ℝ, let w be D004. Starting at s_0=w_0, perform s_{k+1}=(s_k+w_{k+1})(1+δadd_k) for k=0,…,n−1 in increasing order, and return S=s_n. For n=0, return w_0 without any additions.
dependency_coverage.name: Sequential perturbed summation

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Models the individual exponential errors used in both the computed numerator and denominator.

binders: For every n∈ℕ, including n=0, and every x:{0,…,n}→ℝ.
There exist real constants C>0 and u₀>0. They may depend on n and x; they are chosen before u and all error vectors.
For every real u satisfying 0<u≤u₀, and every δexp,δdiv:{0,…,n}→ℝ and δadd:{0,…,n−1}→ℝ satisfying the stated coordinate bounds.
There exists a single vector τ:{0,…,n}→ℝ for the given n,x,u,δexp,δadd,δdiv, satisfying all componentwise conclusions simultaneously and the norm conclusion.
conclusions: For every j∈{0,…,n}, the exact equality ŷ_j=y_j(1+τ_j) holds.
The same constants and bound satisfy ‖y−ŷ‖∞/‖y‖∞≤((n+1)+3)u+C u².
Equivalently, the last inequality is max_{0≤j≤n}|y_j−ŷ_j| divided by max_{0≤j≤n}|y_j|, bounded above by (n+4)u+C u².
hypotheses: The input x is an arbitrary vector of n+1 real numbers; no magnitude, sign, or distinctness restriction is imposed.
There are no further constraints or probabilistic assumptions on the error vectors, and no explicit nonzero-computed-denominator hypothesis.
mathematical_definitions: Use I_n={0,…,n} for Fin(n+1) and A_n={0,…,n−1} for Fin n; A_0 is empty.
Let E_i=exp(x_i) and T=Σ_{i=0}^n E_i. Define the exact normalized exponential vector by y_i=E_i/T.
Define perturbed exponential values by w_i=E_i(1+δexp_i).
Define the sequential computed denominator by s_0=w_0 and s_{k+1}=(s_k+w_{k+1})(1+δadd_k) for k=0,…,n−1, in increasing order; set S=s_n.
Define the computed output by ŷ_j=(w_j/S)(1+δdiv_j). Thus each addition error multiplies the entire updated accumulator, and each division error multiplies its own final quotient.
For a real vector v indexed by I_n, ‖v‖∞=max_{j∈I_n}|v_j|. Function subtraction is coordinatewise.
The coefficient is the real cast of the natural number n+1, plus the real number 3. The power u² has natural exponent 2.
Real division follows Lean's totalized field convention a/0=0; at nonzero denominators it is ordinary real division.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For each natural n and each real input vector x of length n+1, there are positive constants C and u₀, allowed to depend on n and x, such that every error scale 0<u≤u₀ and every collection of exponential, sequential-addition, and final-division multiplicative errors of absolute value at most u produce an output ŷ whose coordinates can all be written exactly as y_j(1+τ_j), where y is the exact normalized exponential vector and |τ_j|≤(n+4)u+C u² for every j. The relative supremum-norm error ‖y−ŷ‖∞/‖y‖∞ obeys the same bound. The constants are uniform over u and all admissible error vectors for the fixed n and x.

vacuity_risks: The small-error range is not empty: u₀>0 permits, for example, u=u₀/2, and zero error vectors satisfy every error hypothesis. Thus the universal implication cannot be made vacuous by taking u₀≤0 or by an impossible error condition.
When n=0, the addition-error domain is empty and its bound is vacuous, but the output domain has one entry and all output conclusions remain substantive.

Totalized division could hide a zero denominator in an unrestricted model. Here the exact denominator T is strictly positive, every y_j is positive, and ‖y‖∞>0, so the relative norm denominator does not cause vacuity.

The computed denominator S is not explicitly assumed nonzero. For u<1, all factors 1+δexp_i and 1+δadd_k are positive, so the recurrence gives S>0. Because u₀ is existential, a witnessing threshold can be reduced to lie below 1; this is an explanatory consequence, not an extra written hypothesis.

The constants C and u₀ are not quantified uniformly over n or x. The statement supplies a local small-u bound for each fixed input and length, with no explicit threshold or quadratic coefficient and no assertion for all positive u.
The conclusion applies to the supplied abstract error model. It does not by itself establish that a particular finite-precision implementation realizes that model.
